item.title: Man United’s risky decision on Chido Obi is backfiring spectacularly
item.description: Man United’s risky decision on Chido Obi is backfiring spectacularly When Manchester United signed Chido Obi in October 2024, he was regarded as one of the most exciting attacking prospects in English football. His goalscoring record with Arsenal’s junior teams was extraordinary. Obi broke Arsenal’s Under-18 scoring record in the 2023/24 season with 32 goals in 18 games, 28 of which came in the final nine matches. He also posted some eye-catching numbers, scoring seven against Norwich, five against West Ham, and four apiece against Crystal Palace and Fulham. Most memorable of all, though, he once scored 10 goals in a single match for Arsenal’s Under-16s against Liverpool in November 2023. In all fairness, the Red Devils were securing a genuine goalscoring magnet, a player who, if everything fell into place, was tipped to become a Premier League defender’s worst nightmare. The young Dane arrived at Carrington and promptly continued his fine scoring run. That form led former United head coach Ruben Amorim to call upon him during the second half of the 2024-25 season amid the club’s injury problems. In 2025-26, however, the club chose not to use him with the senior side, preferring instead to let him develop at Carrington with the junior teams. Yet his prolific 2025-26 campaign, which saw him score 20 goals across all competitions, coupled with clear improvements in hold-up play and pressing out of possession, showed he had outgrown academy football. A loan move was widely expected. Initially, a switch to Bundesliga side FC Köln appeared likely, but no formal offer materialised. Chido Obi joins Willem II on a season-long loan Then, out of nowhere, a less familiar Dutch club stepped forward. Newly promoted Willem II, just back in the Eredivisie, tabled a season-long loan offer. INEOS quickly sanctioned the exit , hoping Obi would take the next step in his development in the Dutch top flight. Instead, the 18-year-old has endured a nightmare loan spell in the Netherlands. Of the 900 minutes of league football available to Willem II players, Obi has been granted just 48, an unmistakably disappointing return. item.title: Urban Meyer reveals what puzzled him about Ohio State's backup QB decision
item.description: When Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin left the game against Indiana on Oct. 17 with an injury, backup true freshman Luke Fahey replaced him. It caught former OSU coach Urban Meyer by surprise. "Once again, I don't have insider information, but when I saw that [Luke] Fahey jogged on the field, I remember going 'Wait a minute, where is [Tavien] St. Clair? What's happening here?'" Meyer said on " The Triple Option " show Oct. 20. Urban Meyer on OSU vs Texas: Urban Meyer identifies biggest concern from Ohio State's collapse vs Texas In Ohio State's preseason camp, OSU coach Ryan Day said that Tavien St. Clair , a former five-star recruit, would split second-team reps with Fahey, a former three-star, in practices. By the time the Ball State game came around on Sept. 5, it was Fahey, not St. Clair, who entered the contest after Sayin's day was done. Fahey played on three drives against the Hoosiers. He finished 0 for 2 on throws with one sack taken and -2 yards rushing. Entering the first drive on second-and-28, Fahey rushed for an eight-yard gain and was hit late by Indiana's Isaiah Jones, resulting in a penalty and a first down. Who should start at QB for Ohio State vs USC? pic.twitter.com/mBjmrqeZ8P — The Triple Option (@3xOptionShow) October 19, 2026 Fahey got the ball back after punting on the first drive, but the Buckeyes went three-and-out and punted again. On his third drive, Fahey kneeled twice after the defense sealed the game by preventing an Indiana score with a minute remaining. With Sayin expected to miss "weeks," according to Day, Meyer believes Ohio State could still start St. Clair. "I'm curious to see if they try the five-star," Meyer said. "I know how talented he is, and it's perplexing why he's not the quarterback and why he doesn't jog on the field when Sayin went down." St. Clair stood out during the spring game in April. The Bellefontaine native was also the first Ohio high school quarterback since Joe Burrow to sign a scholarship agreement with Ohio State. He was a top-10 overall prospect in the 2025 recruiting class and the third-highest-rated quarterback in the modern rankings era to join the Buckeyes. The Buckeyes have an off week before they have to send out a new starter on the road against USC on Oct. 31. item.title: Peta urges Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot
item.description: Peta has called on Crystal Palace to stop using Phoenix, the club's bald eagle mascot, with immediate effect. The animal rights group wrote to Palace CEO Sharon Lacey demanding the club commit to “never using a live animal mascot again”. “Bald eagles are revered as symbols of freedom, yet Phoenix is being used as little more than a prop to entertain football fans,” said Peta's Dr Carys Bennett. "Crystal Palace already has a human mascot to energise supporters, so there's no reason to drag a wild animal into a noisy, crowded stadium. “Peta is urging the club to let Phoenix spread his wings and retire him from matchday duties for good.” PETA has called on Crystal Palace to retire its mascot (AFP/Getty) Peta says that “reclusive eagles deserve better than a stressful, booming stadium environment” where “bright lights, loud noises, and boisterous crowds can cause birds to become frightened, disoriented and panicked”. The letter pointed to other incidents involving live birds at football, including “an owl who died after being hit by a ball, eagles who crashed into walls or glass windows, and a falcon who landed on a fan’s head, sinking his talons into the man’s scalp”. “In another case,” Peta continued, “a rowdy football supporter punched a rival team’s eagle mascot”. That incident is believed to relate to a fan attacking Kayla, Palace's previous eagle mascot, at a League Cup match against south London rivals Charlton in September 2015, a fixture marred by crowd trouble. Kayla regularly appeared before matches at Selhurst Park and flew the length of the pitch. Peta’s request comes as pressure builds on Palace manager Pierre Sage following a difficult start to the season. Palace have taken seven points from their opening seven games and were thrashed 5-0 by local rivals Brighton at the Amex Stadium on Sunday. Diego Gomez scored the pick of the goals as he found the net from the halfway line on an embarrassing afternoon for the Eagles. Palace will aim to bounce back from that loss when they travel to Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday.

item.description: Left to right, Nicole Curran, Joe Lacob, Too Short, Mistah F.A.B. and Peter Gruber sit in the first row during Game 2 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center in San Francisco on Oct. 19, 2026. item.title: JumboMax JMX UltraLong grip offers new way to control distance
item.description: A golf grip usually has one job: give your hands a place to hang on while the rest of the club does something useful. JumboMax’s new JMX UltraLong grip asks it to do a little more. The 15-inch grip is designed to give golfers another hand position on the shaft, creating a third point of contact and another way to control distance. Available for $18.99 each , the JMX UltraLong is longer than a standard grip and lets a player grip at the top, middle or bottom. That extra real estate could be especially useful with short irons and wedges, where golfers often face awkward shots that require them to choke down on the grip and often hold the steel shaft instead of the grip itself. Then there’s distance control. A player can use the top of the grip for a full-length setup, then choke down toward the middle or bottom to change the club’s effective length and control distance. The grip does not make distance control automatic, of course, but it gives players another repeatable option to practice when they are between full-swing distances. JumboMax says the JMX UltraLong has an extra-firm Tour Series skin and is lightweight, so installing one should cause little to no change in a club’s swing weight. It will be offered in three sizes: standard jumbo (+1/8 inch), medium (+5/16 inch) and extra-large (+3/8 inch). The longer grip may suit players who like to choke down on a club, want a consistent reference for different swings or simply find that a conventional grip offers too little room to move their hands. Golfers who already have a dialed-in wedge setup may not need this variable, but for someone who struggles to take distance off scoring clubs without decelerating, the JMX UltraLong offers a small equipment change that could make big differences. David Dusek is a senior writer at Golfweek covering equipment. This article originally appeared on Golfweek: JumboMax JMX UltraLong grip offers new way to control distance

item.title: Sloppy England start winter with Pakistan defeat
item.description: Pakistan have won their first two matches in the tri-series, while England next play Sri Lanka on Thursday [Getty Images] One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi Pakistan 302-9 (50 overs): Baker 3-65; Nawaz 79 (74), Arafat 59 (58) England 215 (38.4 overs): Banton 57 (53), Arafat 6-40 Pakistan won by 87 runs Scorecard England began their wandering winter with a sloppy loss to Pakistan in the one-day tri-series in Rawalpindi. In the opening match of five separate tours to four different countries on three continents, England's mistakes opened the door for Pakistan's Arafat Minhas to take advantage. The all-rounder made a crucial 59 with the bat, then bamboozled England by taking 6-40 with his left-arm spin. Asked to bat, Pakistan were 190-5 in the 37th over when diving wicketkeeper Jordan Cox put down Arafat on 12, one of three catches England dropped. Arafat, alongside a powerful 79 from Hasan Nawaz, lifted Pakistan to 302-9. Faced with making the second-highest score to win an ODI at the Rawalpindi Stadium, England made a rapid start to the chase, only for further errors to let Pakistan back in. At 91-0, Ben Duckett top-edged a pull to depart for 45 and, crucially, Tom Banton was caught for 57 when he shovelled Arafat's long hop to mid-wicket. Arafat's fine all-round performance continued with a beautiful delivery to bowl England captain Harry Brook for five and Naseem Shah got one to keep low to bowl Joe Root for 33. When Cox was lbw and Jamie Overton holed out, both off Arafat, England were floored. They spluttered to 215 all out, losing their last seven wickets for 50 runs, capped by a calamitous run out of Gus Atkinson. Pakistan have two wins from two in the tri-series and are already on the brink of the final, while England next meet Sri Lanka at the same ground on Thursday, with both sides looking for their first victory. Winter and World Cup countdown start with defeat Not only is this the beginning of England's winter – two trips to Australia and Test tours of South Africa and Bangladesh follow – but also the start of a long run-in to the 50-over World Cup in southern Africa next year. This was the first of a potential 21 ODIs in preparation for the World Cup, the tri-series format designed to replicate the pressure and permutations of tournament cricket. Cox dropped two catches behind the stumps, Sonny Baker was expensive with the new ball and Banton squandered the platform to make a huge score at the top of the order. item.title: John Daly once shared the secret to shooting lower scores which Tiger Woods was taught
item.description: Photo by Donald Miralle/Getty Images John Daly is one of the most naturally gifted golfers in the history of the sport, if not the most naturally gifted. Tiger Woods was obviously precociously talented as well, but he worked a lot harder on his game than Daly ever did. Daly and Woods actually enjoyed many thrilling battles with each other throughout the years and, despite the obvious difference in their styles as players and characters, they both have huge respect for one another. John Daly won five times on the PGA Tour, including two major championships, while Tiger Woods is one of the two most successful golfers ever to have graced the game. Daly and Woods have been two of the most explosive and exciting players to watch over the past few decades. However, while both were incredibly long off the tee, their greatest strength was arguably their exceptional short games. John Daly’s secret to shooting lower scores which Tiger Woods was taught During an appearance on the Full Send Podcast , Daly revealed the specific part of the game that amateurs should focus on improving if they want to lower their scores. “ Chipping and putting, for all the amateurs out there. Chipping, putting. “ Daly said. Daly was then told that Tiger Woods’ father, Earl, taught his son to practice exactly the same way when he first started playing. “ He started putting when he was very young, “ Daly replied. “ Then he went to chipping, then he went to 100 yards, then 150 yards or whatever. “ The drivers, everybody in golf that plays can hit a driver, they can hit a five iron, they can hit a six iron. “ But it’s 125, 150 yards in, that means a lot. “ Tiger Woods still spends the majority of his time on the practice area working on his chipping and putting. It’s no coincidence that the 50-year-old has won a record-equalling 82 PGA Tour titles throughout his career, including 15 major championships. If you are an amateur golfer who wants to lower your scores immediately, practicing your chipping and putting is the quickest way to do so.

item.title: Where Oregon Ducks' offense ranks nationally after Week 7 win
item.description: The offense didn't exactly come back to life for the Oregon Ducks in Week 7, but it did put together two long scoring drives in the fourth quarter to ultimately come away with a 17-14 victory over Nebraska . The defense was once again the star of the show, as the Ducks had nothing to show through three quarters. Dan Lanning made the inverse decision from the UCLA game, pulling Brock Thomas in favor of Dylan Raiola to start the fourth quarter, giving Raiola a shot to win the game against the team he led for two seasons. Raiola pulled through, completing 11-of-18 passes for 59 yards and finding Jamari Johnson for the game-winning touchdown with 28 seconds to go. The Ducks didn't have much of a running threat until Raiola entered the game, primarily because the Cornhuskers stacked the box against Thomas, knowing the Ducks wouldn't make him push the ball downfield. Things changed when Raiola entered, however, and the Ducks wound up rushing for 3.4 yards per carry, while Dierre Hill Jr. , Jordon Davison and even freshman Brandon Smith ripped impressive runs. Oregon's offense still has a long way to go to regain the form it had earlier in the season, and getting Dante Moore back in the lineup would surely help. But the Ducks connected with five different receivers on Saturday night, including freshman Jalen Lott , who had three grabs and a key fourth-down conversion on the final drive. Let's take a look at where the Ducks' scoring unit ranks after the Week 7 come-from-behind win against Nebraska and ahead of the team's trip to face Illinois. item.title: Ex-NFL coach praises Giants’ J.J. McCarthy: ‘Best we’ve seen’ from him
item.description: J.J. McCarthy ’s performance on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints was the “best we’ve seen him on an NFL field,” according to former Jets and Buffalo Bills coach Rex Ryan. McCarthy relieved Jameis Winston with the Giants trailing 34-10, and the Giants proceeded to score 17 fourth-quarter points in a 34-27 loss. item.title: McLaren to sell F1 cars driven by Hamilton and Senna with lofty asking price
item.description: McLaren are set to auction off five Formula 1 cars, including models driven by former world champions Lewis Hamilton , Ayrton Senna and reigning champ Lando Norris . The five cars could raise tens of millions of pounds, with asking prices per model expected to be between £5m and £10m. They will be sold through Tom Hartley Jnr. Among the models are the last McLaren driven by Lewis Hamilton in 2012, the MP4/27A, as well as two models of the MP4/6A cars tested by Senna in 1991 and driven by Gerhard Berger. Gerhard Berger drove the 1991 McLaren car (Getty) Two recent models driven by Norris, the 2021 MCL35M and 2023 MCL60, will also be sold to the highest bidder. “We have decided to part with these iconic McLaren Formula One cars because we feel that having them simply sitting in storage is a disservice to what they represent,” said McLaren F1 CEO Zak Brown. “These cars were built to be driven and raced, and we want to see them being used and enjoyed. We believe that is the best way to keep our history alive and our heritage business active.” For comparison, Hamilton’s 2010 McLaren car, the MP4-25A, was sold for £4.8mollion in 2021 while Michael Schumacher’s championship-winning 2001 Ferrari car was sold for £5.6m in 2017. The 2023 McLaren car was also driven by Brad Pitt in Austin as he learned to drive an F1 car in connection with his leading role in the 2025 film, F1 . The moment Brad Pitt took on the challenge of an F1 car with McLaren 🔥 pic.twitter.com/hGEEra7RRE — Sky Sports F1 (@SkySportsF1) June 27, 2025 Hartley, who previously sold Bernie Ecclestone’s collection of cars, added: “It is incredibly rare for a collector to have the opportunity to acquire race-driven grand prix cars directly from the manufacturer and team that built and campaigned them, and that makes this a very special offering. “These five cars will be offered individually and there is no time pressure whatsoever. Our priority, and McLaren’s, is to find the right homes for them.”

item.title: Uefa demands Fifa releases documents relating to World Cup sell-off scheme
item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
